subject.notes: subject begins on the dominant; answer begins on tonic, harmonized in tonic until bar 6; only bars 4 and 21 use the answer form. Ch.2 p.6 lists I.11 among subjects beginning on the dominant whose answer begins on the tonic and is otherwise real. (The diatonic-auxiliary remark on p.6 concerns II.11, not I.11; the OCR reads it as I.11.)

claims.claim: The subject ends at the first note of bar 4; a codetta incorporating the rising scale of bar 2 leads to the CS in bar 5 (bar numbering starts at 0 for the upbeat).
The subject can be used in canon with itself at the octave after two bars; all three stretti are of this type.
Stretto 1 prolongs the counterexposition; stretto 2 in vi (soprano 36, middle 38, bass 40); stretto 3 in ii in reverse order (bass 46, middle 48, soprano 50); both extended toward cadences.
Of fourteen entries only two (bars 4 and 21) use the answer form.
Not radically different in form from Group 2 fugues; uses groups of stretto entries in place of single entries.
I.11 and I.15 subjects combine with themselves in canon at the octave; Bach used only this type of stretto in them.
